findings.title: Production rejects default or short signing secrets
findings.evidence: Development retains an explicit local fallback, while production startup rejects the default or secrets shorter than 32 characters.

findings.title: CORS uses an explicit configurable allowlist
findings.evidence: CORS origins are environment-configurable, wildcard origins are rejected, and methods/headers are explicitly bounded.

findings.title: Refresh token is not persisted by frontend JavaScript
findings.evidence: frontend/assets/js/api.js keeps only a compatibility reader and removes old refresh-token localStorage values.

findings.title: Refresh cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite, and Secure-configurable
findings.evidence: auth router sets ai_nav_refresh_token as HttpOnly and uses config-driven SameSite/Secure settings.

findings.title: Auth and users routers contain no SQL
findings.evidence: Router SQL keyword scan.

findings.title: Users request DTOs forbid extra fields
findings.evidence: Auth/users request models inherit the shared StrictModel.

findings.title: Password change and reset revoke active sessions
findings.evidence: Security/authentication repositories revoke sessions after password changes.

findings.title: Password hashes are versioned and upgraded after successful reauth
findings.evidence: Password hash rounds are configurable, login upgrades legacy hashes, and sensitive security-question reauth also refreshes stale hashes.

findings.title: Login failures are counted and temporarily locked without account-state disclosure
findings.evidence: Login service applies a configurable temporary lock while preserving the same external INVALID_CREDENTIALS error.

findings.title: Sessions identify the current device and support revoking other devices
findings.evidence: Sessions API marks current sessions from the refresh cookie, returns risk state, and exposes revoke-others.

findings.title: Avatar ingestion validates image content and rolls back stored files
findings.evidence: Avatar processing is owned by Users/profile, validates declared and decoded formats plus pixel count, writes atomically, and removes new files when profile persistence fails.

findings.title: Learning, Tools, and Agent consume preferences through the Users facade
findings.evidence: Consumers read projected preference contexts from Users; Agent rejects copied client preference state and consumer adapters contain no direct user-table access.

findings.title: Backend permission dependency enforces RBAC for protected domain commands
findings.evidence: Authorization service returns stable 403 decisions and FastAPI dependencies protect Agent and private learning-state routes.

findings.title: Sensitive user commands use registered audit events and allowlisted metadata
findings.evidence: Users write routes emit registered audit events whose metadata is filtered by event allowlists and sensitive-key denial.

findings.title: Account deletion uses staged retention and controlled anonymization
findings.evidence: Deletion requests are unique and staged through grace, soft-delete, recovery retention, and admin-authorized anonymization without deleting public domain facts.

findings.title: Agent memory requires current versioned consent
findings.evidence: Append-only consent events carry policy versions; stale consent is rejected and Agent context checks the current consent rather than the legacy preference flag.

findings.title: User data export requires reauthentication and excludes authentication secrets
findings.evidence: Export requires the current password, emits an audit event, and its response projections omit password, refresh-token, and security-answer hashes.

findings.title: Workflow assets use user ownership, stable references, versions, and idempotency
findings.evidence: Users owns versioned workflow assets; idempotency is scoped to the user and external tool references are not cascade-coupled.

findings.title: Agent workflow writes require confirmation and use the Users command facade
findings.evidence: Agent cannot write asset tables directly; save commands require explicit confirmation, an idempotency key, and registered Users audit events.

findings.title: Agent context is minimal and unavailable targets remain visible
findings.evidence: Agent receives only preferences, capability flags, and an asset summary; retired targets are represented as unavailable without deleting the saved workflow.

findings.title: Users access logs are structured and exclude request PII and secrets
findings.evidence: Observed requests log only a sanitized request ID, route operation, status, latency, and error code; request bodies, identity fields, headers, and secrets are not read.

findings.title: Operational metrics are aggregated and administrator-authorized
findings.evidence: The metrics endpoint requires users:manage and returns operation counters and threshold alerts without labels containing user identity.

findings.title: Database backups and restores are integrity-checked and atomically replaced
findings.evidence: Online backups and restored files are verified, replacement is atomic, prior targets are preserved, and rehearsal confirms migration checksums plus a restored canary.

findings.title: Database startup uses lifespan and deployment health probes
findings.evidence: Database initialization runs in FastAPI lifespan, the database path is injectable, liveness has no dependency, and readiness verifies database access plus applied migrations.

findings.title: Authentication compatibility DDL is versioned and transactional
findings.evidence: Legacy auth schema repair is migration 008 with checksum tracking; conditional column work runs under the migration lock and ad hoc startup DDL has been removed.

findings.title: Authentication endpoints use persistent hashed rate limits and trusted proxy boundaries
findings.evidence: Rate limits are atomically persisted with HMAC subject keys and Retry-After; forwarded addresses are ignored unless the direct peer belongs to an explicit trusted proxy CIDR.

findings.title: Frontend access-token refresh is single-flight and cookie-based
findings.evidence: Concurrent 401 responses share one refresh promise using the HttpOnly cookie, retry once, and clear local access state when refresh fails.

findings.title: Every Users command declares audit, replay, and concurrency controls
findings.evidence: The route-derived registry covers every Users/Auth command with semantic audit, replay, and concurrency controls; authentication lifecycle events are allowlisted and emitted without secrets.
